ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: the road league, the hospitallers and the herders
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Rimfolk adds three peoples of peaceful callings to the world: a road league of caravan masters and waystation keepers, an order of hospitallers who keep sickhouses, and nomad herders who follow the grass with great herds. Each has its own gear, colours, faith, towns and words, and turns up in Rimfolk's camps, asks, callers and letters in its own way.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: They are among the world's peoples when a new world is made, once each, at the game's usual chances; remove them in the world's faction list like any other people. A save made before they were there meets them when one of them arises during play (the page on new peoples that arise). Four more came later: the pilgrims, the scholars, the spacer enclave and the river folk have a page of their own.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: All three are mostly peaceful. They defend their towns, and they raid only when the colony has turned them hostile, by the game's own rules, and less often than other peoples then. Their notables have titles of their own, their messengers words of their own, and their towns a plan of their own when the land suits it.

li.heading: Who they are

table.li: People | Lives by | Age | On the map | Their towns
The road league | Trade on the roads | Industrial | Coats dyed teal of every cut; guards in one kit of duster, hat and flak | Few: walled waystations where roads meet
The hospitaller order | Healing | Medieval | An ivory habit of any cut; sworn guards in ivory plate, lay archers | Sickhouses round an herb garden
The herding folk | Their herds | Tribal | Hides of every make, russet caps and coats; wardens in war veils | Camps of round houses and pens

li.after: With Ideology each keeps a faith of its own (a creed of the road, the open hand, the long grass) and its own style; with Biotech each has a share of other kinds of people (hussars and genies with the league, yttakin and pigskins with the herders). With Vanilla Ideology Expanded's memes their faiths take a meme of trade, of healthcare or of nomads too.

li.heading: What they wear, carry and know
li.text: No two of them look alike, but each people is known by its colour on a piece or two. Their soldiers wear one kit, their civilians whatever their age and calling would, drawn from the game, the DLCs and the mods loaded (the Vanilla Expanded apparel, armour, accessories and weapons sets, Vanilla Factions Expanded's medieval, tribal and settlers' gear). With no mods at all the base game's gear dresses and arms every one of them. Pawns already in a game keep what they have; new ones come dressed this way.

points.li: The road league: wayfarers and factors in a teal coat of any cut over travelling clothes, with frontier revolvers and rifles where Vanilla Weapons Expanded's Frontier set is loaded; caravan guards and outriders in the league's kit of teal duster, cowboy hat and flak; wayfarers carry beer, cloth or a little silver. A few of the guards and outriders are sharpshooters or gladiators of A RimWorld of Magic, and now and then the league master is a commander.

The hospitaller order: the habit is shared but not its cut or its age, an ivory robe or mantle worn thin or new, with a hood, a cap or now and then a plague doctor's mask; the sworn guards in matching ivory plate and helmet, with Medieval 2 the order's ivory tabard and a heater shield; the lay archers in an ivory cape and helmet with a quiver. Hospitallers carry herbs and clean cloth. Some of the hospitallers and their prior are priests of A RimWorld of Magic, a few of the sworn guards paladins.

The herding folk: hides and wraps of every make, russet on their tail caps, wraps and coats; their herd wardens in war veils and war wraps; archers with quivers, herders with slings. Herders carry hay or hides. Their elder is often a druid, a few archers are rangers.

Their kinds of people (Biotech) are a real mix, and still mostly baseliners: genies, highmates, lowmates, drakonori and high elves among the hospitallers; yttakin, neanderthals, animusen, boarskins, venators, saurids and wood elves with the herders; hussars, genies, boglegs, stoneborn, uhlans, starjacks and a few androids on the league's roads, each where its mod is loaded.

The road league: when the game sends a trader caravan, the league's is three times as likely as another people's, with rich and varied stock and plenty of guards. Its market folk, salt caravans, far merchants and road wardens camp on the colony's land more often. An outrider may come ahead of a caravan to ask whether it should turn aside to the colony, and the league may ask the colony's caravan to walk one of its factors home with the season's silver.

The hospitaller order: its healers, herb-gatherers, pilgrims and penitents camp more often. One of its hospitallers may stop at the gate for a colonist with an everyday ailment and see to it for nothing; the colony may send medicine back for the sickhouse. In a plague year the order asks the colony for medicine by a set day, and a call for a healer to help at a sickhouse comes from the order likeliest. Travellers who lodge at one of its sickhouses come home tended, as if they had carried medicine.

The herding folk: their caravans walk a herd of eight to fourteen beasts for sale beside their pack animals, and come half again as often. Their drovers, shearers and beast-catchers camp more often, and in the fall and the winter they ask to graze a herd of up to a dozen head on the colony's land for the cold months. The drove roads and the great herds come for them likeliest, and the ask for fodder for a herd; a herder at the gate with a thirsty or sick herd, or drovers on the way to a fair, likeliest are theirs.
Their towns' heads are waymasters, priors and prioresses, and camp elders; their traders are caravan masters, cellarers and drovers; their messengers are road riders, postulants and riders.
Their letters, their messengers at the gate and the talk with them are in their own voice, as each people's age is in its own.

A town of theirs, when its map is made, is laid out to their plan: the league's walled yard with stalls and a storehouse, the order's long ward of sixteen beds and its cloister, the herders' round houses and two great pens with their herd in them. Where the land is too wet or rough for it, the game makes its own base.
